title: Dr. and Mrs. Frank Chin v. Covenant Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1: No—the Session did not err in its understanding and application of BCO 57-2 in denying the Chins' request to examine their young children for admission to the sealing ordinances. Issue 2: No—Covenant Presbytery did not err in denying the Chins' complaint. The complaint was not sustained; six members dissented.
first_summary: The Chins complained that Covenant Presbytery wrongly denied their complaint against the Covenant Presbyterian Church Session's refusal to examine their young children for admission to the Lord's Supper. The SJC denied the complaint. It held that BCO 57-2 gives the Session discretion over when to examine a child and does not require examination of every child; if examination occurs, it must be careful. A dissent argued BCO 57-1 required examination of covenant children seeking admission.
summary: The Chins complained to the SJC after Covenant Presbytery denied their complaint against Covenant Presbyterian Church Session's refusal to examine their young children for admission to the Lord's Supper. The SJC did not sustain the complaint. Its adopted reasoning held that BCO 57-2 leaves the time for examining young persons to the Session's prudence and imposes no mandate to examine every child put forward; if the Session decides the time has come, careful examination is required. The dissent read BCO 57-1 as requiring examination of covenant children seeking admission.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2003-04, SJC, 33rd GA (2005), adopted judgment at lines 74–94; reasoning by RE Terry Jones at line 92; vote 14 concur/7 dissent/1 recused/2 absent at line 94.
evidence_notes.dispute: The Chins asked the CPC Session to examine their young children for admission to the Lord's Supper; the Session declined (lines 36–38), Presbytery denied the complaint (lines 44–52), and the Chins filed with the SJC (lines 54–72).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Judgment answers No to both issues (lines 74–78); adopted reasoning holds BCO 57-2 does not mandate examination of every young person and leaves timing to Session prudence, but requires careful examination if the Session determines the time has come (lines 84–90).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Six members dissented (lines 98–147), arguing BCO 57-1 requires the Session to honor covenant children's desire to seek admission by examining them; the dissent was not adopted.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision is incorporated by reference; the Presbytery's denial is summarized in the chronology and issues (lines 44–52, 72).
